policy: Every node must be traceable to observations/sources and carry an explicit geometry-authority boundary.

nodes.subject: khafre_pyramid
nodes.label: Official original-height summary
nodes.caveat: Official summary coexists with detailed survey reconstruction.

nodes.subject: khafre_pyramid
nodes.label: Core/backing stone
nodes.value: Local fossiliferous limestone
nodes.caveat: Material context does not write block geometry.

nodes.subject: khafre_pyramid
nodes.label: Casing system
nodes.value: Fine Tura limestone survives at upper levels; published materials study reports granite at base courses
nodes.caveat: Course-by-course extent still requires survey evidence.

nodes.subject: khafre_pyramid
nodes.label: Casing-foundation orientation prior
nodes.value: -4.45 arcmin derived rigid-square prior
nodes.caveat: Translation/elevation unresolved; individual side residuals retained.

nodes.subject: khafre_interior
nodes.label: Belzoni entry date
nodes.value: 2 March 1818
nodes.caveat: Historical event only.

nodes.subject: khafre_burial_chamber
nodes.label: Burial chamber roof form
nodes.value: Rock-excavated chamber with angular/gabled compact-stone roof blocks
nodes.caveat: Modern metric geometry requires survey confirmation.

nodes.subject: khafre_sarcophagus
nodes.label: Sarcophagus setting
nodes.value: Sunk into western floor zone with surrounding granite and granite bedding slab
nodes.caveat: Do not infer hidden passages from nineteenth-century analogy.

nodes.subject: khafre_lower_chamber
nodes.label: Historic water stain
nodes.value: Perring reported an approximately 12-inch water-stain height
nodes.caveat: Not a modern groundwater level or evidence of a hydraulic system.

nodes.subject: khafre_valley_temple
nodes.label: Valley Temple materials
nodes.value: Massive limestone blocks encased in granite, alabaster floors, monolithic granite pillars
nodes.caveat: Detailed stone-by-stone provenance needs ARCE/survey records.

nodes.subject: khafre_valley_temple
nodes.label: Digital Giza find inventory
nodes.value: 17 indexed finds
nodes.caveat: Catalog count, not excavation-total completeness.

nodes.subject: khafre_pyramid_temple
nodes.label: Digital Giza find inventory
nodes.value: 5 indexed finds
nodes.caveat: Catalog count, not excavation-total completeness.

nodes.subject: khafre_pyramid_temple
nodes.label: Khafre named architrave
nodes.value: Original red-granite architrave bears Khafre titulary; probable pyramid-temple origin; later reused at Lisht
nodes.caveat: Probable original placement remains curatorial reconstruction.

nodes.subject: great_sphinx
nodes.label: Fabric
nodes.value: Carved directly from Giza bedrock
nodes.caveat: No metric geometry authority.

nodes.subject: great_sphinx
nodes.label: Khafre attribution
nodes.value: Evidence strongly favors Khafre-period construction
nodes.caveat: Strong support is not mathematical proof; preserve alternative claims separately.

nodes.subject: khafre_lower_complex
nodes.label: Relative sequence
nodes.value: Valley Temple precedes Sphinx Temple; causeway precedes Sphinx quarry
nodes.caveat: Relative sequence, not absolute calendar date.

nodes.subject: sphinx_temple
nodes.label: Quarry-construction link
nodes.value: AERA/ARCE geological mapping links Sphinx-quarry strata to Sphinx Temple core blocks
nodes.caveat: Block-source matching is expert interpretation based on mapped strata.

nodes.subject: area_c
nodes.label: Gallery function
nodes.value: Re-excavation favors storage/craft use rather than worker barracks
nodes.caveat: Does not by itself identify all occupants/workforce organization.

nodes.subject: giza_plateau
nodes.label: Plateau geomorphology
nodes.value: Pliocene cliff-line context with lithology, joints and faults as morphogenetic controls
nodes.caveat: Regional geological context; not a deep-void model.

nodes.subject: old_kingdom_chronology
nodes.label: Radiocarbon program
nodes.value: More than 450 organic samples collected across Old/Middle Kingdom monuments
nodes.caveat: Not all samples are Khafre-specific.

nodes.subject: old_kingdom_chronology
nodes.label: Old-wood caveat
nodes.value: Reused/old wood can bias charcoal ages older than construction event
nodes.caveat: Radiocarbon offsets must not be read as direct proof of earlier pyramid construction.

nodes.subject: giza_plateau
nodes.label: World Heritage context
nodes.value: Giza lies within UNESCO property 86, inscribed 1979
nodes.caveat: Heritage status, not archaeological proof.

nodes.subject: khafre_pyramid
nodes.label: Facade fracture monitoring
nodes.value: 2009–2012 photographic documentation with in-situ verification of major cracks in 2012
nodes.caveat: Does not establish ancient crack origin or hidden geometry.

nodes.subject: khafre_pyramid
nodes.label: ScIDEP status
nodes.value: 2025 peer-reviewed paper documents project design/construction and planned multi-view muography; not a finished hidden-void result
nodes.caveat: Method/project status only; no hidden-space claim promotion.

nodes.subject: khafre_surface
nodes.label: 2025 laser survey
nodes.value: AERA bibliography records a first laser survey of the Second Great Pyramid; underlying geometry data remain pending access
nodes.caveat: Existence of publication does not authorize point-cloud geometry.

nodes.subject: khafre_complex
nodes.label: Open visual evidence
nodes.value: Rights-reviewed Commons assets plus Digital Giza catalog surface provide multi-date visual evidence
nodes.caveat: Photos remain visual observations until camera registration and residual QA.

nodes.subject: old_kingdom_royal_pyramid_complex
nodes.label: Royal funeral / afterlife transition function
nodes.value: Royal pyramid complexes functioned as settings for funeral, procession and preparation of the deceased king for the afterlife.
nodes.caveat: Functional interpretation applies to the royal pyramid-complex tradition; it does not identify every Khafre architectural detail with one ritual act.

nodes.subject: old_kingdom_royal_pyramid_complex
nodes.label: Post-burial royal offering cult
nodes.value: After burial, priests used pyramid-complex spaces to maintain offerings and ritual service for the deceased king.
nodes.caveat: This supports continuing cult function, not a claim that every surviving room has a securely identified ritual use.

nodes.subject: old_kingdom_royal_pyramid_tradition
nodes.label: Solar kingship context
nodes.value: Old Kingdom pyramid architecture participated in an ideological environment of increasingly prominent solar kingship.
nodes.caveat: General Old Kingdom context is not a Khafre-specific inscription proving a particular encoded solar message.

nodes.subject: old_kingdom_state
nodes.label: Centralized-state context
nodes.value: The pyramid-building environment operated within a highly centralized royal state capable of planned monumental landscapes and concentrated administration.
nodes.caveat: State capacity explains coordination context; it does not by itself establish the monument’s religious meaning.

nodes.subject: khafre_valley_temple
nodes.label: Repeated royal statuary in Valley Temple
nodes.value: Multiple Khafre statues/fragments are cataloged from the Valley Temple; official museum record describes one 168 cm diorite statue as one of about 23 similar statues.
nodes.caveat: Presence of statuary does not by itself reconstruct exact statue positions or a unique ritual action.

nodes.subject: khafre_valley_temple
nodes.label: Kingship/unification iconography
nodes.value: Official museum description links the enthroned Khafre image with sema-tawy unification symbolism and Horus protection.
nodes.caveat: Iconographic meaning belongs to the statue/object context and cannot be projected onto every temple action.

nodes.subject: khafre_causeway
nodes.label: Statuary find associated with causeway
nodes.value: Digital Giza indexes a limestone statue head as a Khafre Causeway find.
nodes.caveat: Find association does not establish original display position or processional use.

nodes.subject: khafre_pyramid_temple
nodes.label: Royal titulary at court doorway
nodes.value: Met curatorial reconstruction places Khafre’s cartouche on a red-granite architrave spanning a court doorway, with falcon/statue imagery associated with the piers.
nodes.caveat: Exact original pier/doorway placement requires primary excavation/plan reconciliation.

nodes.subject: khafre_pyramid_temple
nodes.label: Royal statuary in pyramid temple
nodes.value: Digital Giza indexes a lower part of a diorite striding statue of Khafre and another statue fragment among five finds from the pyramid temple.
nodes.caveat: Find inventory does not establish exact ancient placement.

nodes.subject: old_kingdom_royal_pyramid_complex
nodes.label: Offerings/readings directed to royal images
nodes.value: Digital Giza describes living priests presenting offerings and religious readings to statues of the deceased king as part of the post-burial royal offering cult.
nodes.caveat: General Old Kingdom royal-complex function; exact Khafre room-by-room rite remains unresolved.

nodes.subject: khafre_valley_temple
nodes.label: Dual east entrance with goddess associations
nodes.value: The east façade is reconstructed with two entrances; source synthesis associates Bastet with the north entrance and Hathor with the south.
nodes.caveat: Associated flanking sphinx/lion reconstruction remains interpretive.

nodes.subject: khafre_valley_temple_t_hall
nodes.label: 23-position Valley Temple statuary field
nodes.value: The T-shaped hall preserves/reports 23 floor niches, with a 3/7/3/7/3 arrangement in Seidel’s reconstruction.
nodes.caveat: Specific statue-to-niche assignments remain reconstructed.

nodes.subject: khafre_pyramid_temple
nodes.label: Pyramid Temple room program
nodes.value: Independent scholarly synthesis and Hölscher’s excavation monograph converge on pillared halls, a court, five chapel/serdab-like cult spaces, side/magazine spaces and a western inner zone.
nodes.caveat: Exact room outlines require plan-byte parsing and modern survey reconciliation.

nodes.subject: khafre_pyramid_temple_statue_court
nodes.label: Statue-court reconstruction remains non-unique
nodes.value: Physical emplacement evidence supports major statuary/stone installations, but statue type/pose and exact court reconstruction differ among Hölscher, Ricke, Arnold and Jánosi.
nodes.caveat: Do not render one disputed reconstruction as canonical ancient reality.

nodes.subject: khafre_lower_complex
nodes.label: Room topology is ahead of metric plan custody
nodes.value: Room-level topology can now be source-addressed, while the highest-value 1:100 ARCE Valley Temple plan and key Hölscher plates are not yet checksum-bound local source bytes.
nodes.caveat: Topology must remain schematic until source bytes and metric frame receipts exist.

nodes.subject: khafre_plan_sources
nodes.label: Two primary plan families are acquisition-ready or remotely accessible
nodes.value: Petrie 1883 is available as a public-domain scan and Perring Part II is available as a digitized plate volume; neither is locally checksum-bound in this release.
nodes.caveat: Availability is not registration. No plan receives metric authority until local bytes, checksums, scale/frame parse and holdout residuals exist.

nodes.subject: khafre_valley_temple_pillared_hall
nodes.label: Valley Temple light/material/image staging is now a falsifiable candidate
nodes.value: Hölscher’s description links polished granite/alabaster, statue positions and high-aperture light in the Valley Temple hall. Registered openings and wall geometry could test whether the reconstructed reveal/light field is physically plausible.
nodes.caveat: No photometric claim, emotional-effect claim or ritual meaning is established.
